About three-quarters of the tickets for "Monopoly 200X" are sold. The top prize count has held, with two of ten still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "Monopoly 200X" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
696.headline: Top prizes are still left

762.body:
The key fact about "Billion" is how its nine prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

The most common prize left on "Billion" right now is $100.

If "Billion" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
762.headline: Same price, different prizes

827.body:
"50th Anniversary" is down to one top prize after a $15 million winner was claimed last week. The game started with three top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Every line of 50th Anniversary's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
827.headline: The top prize list got shorter

847.body:
Before you buy "Bingo 50X", know that its $500,000 top prize is gone. The game still pays many smaller prizes, but the biggest one left is $100,000. That is a good win, but far from the advertised top prize.

The numbers for "Bingo 50X" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
847.headline: No top prizes remain

891.body:
The most common win left on "Cash Explosion 25X" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If "Cash Explosion 25X" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
891.headline: A close look at the prizes
